chapter_theme: The opening of the Sivavakkiyam: after an invocation of Namasivaya and of the elephant-faced god, Sivavakkiyar sets the five letters, the breath raised to the skull and the One known within against everything done outside, running to shrines, reciting the Vedas, bathing at the three twilights, building houses and sacrificing. The body is a boat that breaks and a corpse the cremation keeper takes; what holds is the one letter among the five, the name repeated, and the feet of the Lord and the Mother.
structure_note: The editorial section labels (அக்ஷர நிலை, சரியை விலக்கல், யோக நிலை, தேகநிலை, ஞான நிலை, கிரியை நிலை) are a modern editor's and not the poet's; the verses are not grouped by them in the text. Two invocations (964, 965) open the work; 974 to 976 and later 1022 are the ராம verses, unexpected in a Saiva poet and read by tradition as cipher. Several verses close on the same oath line, அம்மைபாதம் உண்மையே (968, 986).

964.reading: The poet opens with the rare Namasivaya that is beginning and end, the mantra the gods uttered of old, and says that meditating on the curled letter he will speak the Sivavakkiyam so that fault, sin and maya run far away.
964.nuance: ஆறிரண்டு நூறு தேவர் is a number of gods (twelve hundred, or six and two hundred); the count is formulaic and recurs at 981. சுரியதோர் எழுத்து, the curled letter, is taken by tradition as Om (whose written form curls) or as the five letters held as one; the verse does not say which.

965.reading: Worshipping the wish-granting tree with the black face (the elephant-faced god) so that arts, books and knowledge rise in thought, the poet asks all who have learned, great and small, to forgive the errors of one who recites like a madman.
965.nuance: The invocation follows the convention of beginning with Ganapati, and the apology (பேயனாகி ஓதிடும்) is the poet's own self-description as possessed or mad, a stance he keeps throughout. Grammatically the line can also make the learned themselves the mad reciters; the apology reading fits a preface better.

966.reading: Within the five letters are the cosmos and what is beyond it, the three primal gods, the letters A and MA; within the five letters everything is contained.
966.nuance: அகாரமும் மகாரமும் name two of the three letters of Om, so the pranava is placed inside the five letters rather than above them. The claim that the five letters hold the cosmos is the Tirumanthiram's too.

967.reading: Running and running, seeking and seeking the light that is mingled within, their days passed, they withered and withered and died: people in crores beyond counting.
967.nuance: The whole verse is four repeated words. உட்கலந்த சோதி (the light mingled within) is the point: what they ran after was inside them. The editor's label reads the verse as a rejection of outward chariyai; the verse itself only shows the futility and the count of the dead.

968.reading: If by thought you can hold the breath that is contracting in the formed channel and raise it to the skull, the old become children and the body reddens; this is true, by the feet of the Lord of grace and of the Mother.
968.nuance: The sense turns on உருத்தரித்த நாடி (the channel that has taken form) and கபாலம் ஏற்றல் (raising to the skull); tradition takes the channel as the central one and the raising as the breath carried to the crown. The claim of renewed youth and a reddened body is the classic siddhi of breath, as in Tirumanthiram 805; the closing oath on the two feet recurs at 986 and 1033.

969.reading: A man who sees another desire the woman he has taken says he will cut him down first; yet when the Arbiter comes and calls, this fine body stinks, and they carry it only as far as the cremation ground and hand it to the keeper.
969.nuance: நடுவன் (the arbiter) is Yama, and தோட்டி the cremation-ground keeper, of low caste; the body that was fought over is handed to the one its owner would have shunned. The verse pairs jealousy over a body with the body's end.

970.reading: The One that was in me I did not know; after I came to know the One in me, who else could see it? Staying and staying within myself, I perceived it.
970.nuance: Line 3 can be read as 'who could see it (but I)?' or as 'who is able to see it?' in general. Either way the knowledge is in-dwelling and not transferable, and the verse gives no method beyond இருந்திருந்து, staying within.

971.reading: I find nothing to think of; there is nothing but you. Is the maya that stands as remembering and forgetting really maya? You who are everything, boundless, beginningless before the beginningless: how is it that you are within me and I within you?
971.nuance: நின்றமாயை மாயையோ can be a doubt (is it maya at all?) or a wondering exclamation. The last line is a question, not a statement of union; the mutual indwelling is asked about, not explained.

972.reading: You are the earth, the sky, the seven rolling seas; you are number and letter and the letters of tuned song; you are the eye, the pupil, the image that dances in the eye; grant that I reach your feet, which stand in the nature of what draws near.
972.nuance: The catalogue moves from the world to writing and music to the seeing eye itself: the Lord is the seer as well as the seen. Compare 1024 and 1025, which run the same நீ list.

973.reading: Not Hari, not Brahma, beyond the beyond; the cause that stands past black, red and white; not great, not small; hold to it, hold to it; beyond even turiya, far, far, far.
973.nuance: கருமை செம்மை வெண்மை (black, red, white) are taken by tradition either as the colours of Vishnu, Brahma and Rudra, matching line 1, or as the three gunas; both leave the cause beyond the triad. துரியமும் கடந்து places it beyond the fourth state. The verse is apophatic until the imperative பற்றுமின்கள், which asks for holding on to what cannot be grasped.

974.reading: The bathing at dusk, dawn and noon, the twilight oblations, the austerities and the recitations, the knowledge sought in the mind, the mantra recited daily: all of them are the name 'Rama Rama Rama Rama', my father.
974.nuance: The sense turns on ராம. Read plainly it is the Vaishnava name, surprising in a Saiva Siddhar, and some take 974 to 976 and 1022 as evidence of a different hand. Tradition reads ரா and ம as a cipher for the two breaths or for fire and moon, so that the name is the breath. The verse's own claim is only that this one name does what all the rites do.

975.reading: The mantra that casts off the five great sins: the poor who go about saying 'this is it, this is it, no, it is not', the good mantra for those who recite without ceasing is this, this: the name 'Rama Rama Rama'.
975.nuance: பஞ்ச பாதகம் are the five great sins of the dharma texts. இதாம் இதாம் அதல்ல mocks the search from one mantra to another; the answer repeats the same words as a settled 'this is it'.

976.reading: What is I, what is you, what stands between? What is the king, what is the guru, tell me, slaves! What is it that came to be, what perishes, what is beyond the beyond, what is the low? The name 'Rama Rama Rama'.
976.nuance: A chain of questions answered by the name; whether the name is the answer to each or dismisses the questions is open. குலாமர் (slaves) is the poet's address to those bound to outward authority, as at 998.

977.reading: Sattanatha Bhattar who recites the sastras: when sweat and gasping come, will the Veda come to your help? If you can know within yourself for the space of a maatra and hold together, where is the disease of the scripture-bag? Sakti, mukti, siddhi.
977.nuance: சட்டநாத பட்டர் may be a named Brahmin or a type. மாத்திரைப்போது is a measure of time and also of breath, so line 3 may mean a moment's knowing or a breath held. சாத்திரப்பை நோய், the sastra-bag disease, is the poet's coinage for learning carried as a burden. The closing three words are a list, not a sentence.

978.reading: You recite the four Vedas but do not know the foot of knowledge; like ghee hidden in milk, sinners, you do not know it; while the one who ate the poison is within your heart you speak of Death, and not even in a dream is that so.
978.nuance: ஞானபாதம் is the foot of knowledge, the fourth pada of the Agamas and also the Lord's foot. The ghee in milk is the Tirumanthiram's figure for the Lord unseen within. The last line denies Death any reality for one who has the Lord within.

979.reading: There is no tradition without a seed, above or below; how could a mansion stand without a carpenter? Fools who sell the mother that bore you and buy slaves! Without consciousness there is no life, none at all.
979.nuance: வித்து (seed) and தச்சன் (carpenter) argue from cause to a first cause. பெற்றதாயை விற்று அடிமை கொள்ளுதல், selling one's own mother to buy a slave, is taken by tradition as abandoning the primal Sakti or the inner source for lesser gods or for outward authority; the verse does not gloss it. சித்து is consciousness, and the last line makes it the condition of life.

980.reading: The beginningless mantra that is five and three and is not reached: if you think of it in your heart and recite it until you take its form, even a hundred crore of the five great sins fly off like cotton, so the four Vedas declare.
980.nuance: அஞ்சும் மூணும் எட்டாதாய் puns on எட்டு: five and three make eight, and the mantra is 'unreachable'. Tradition reads the eight as the five letters with the three of Om, or as an eight-syllable mantra. நீருருச் செபிப்பீரேல் may be 'recite till you become it' or 'recite (while) you are water' (that is, at bathing). Compare 1022, which again joins five and three in one letter.

981.reading: A thousand gates of the cosmos, a thousand fierce gates, a thousand gates that are twelve hundred crore; this gate is the poor one's gate, become a single enjoyment; who can see the gate where our Lord is?
981.nuance: வாசல் (gate) is Sivavakkiyar's running cipher (1027, 1031, 1032, 1036, 1037): the womb-door, the body's openings, and the one inner door by which the Lord is reached. ஏழைவாசல் may be the gate of the poor, that is the body, or of the poet himself; ஏகபோகம் is single enjoyment or union. The verse asks the question and does not place the gate.

982.reading: Though you recite the Sama and the four Vedas and all the sastras in safety, you do not know Siva; after you leave the disease of lust and perceive him within your thought, our Lord stays as a mute body.
982.nuance: ஊமையான காயமாய் இருப்பன் is hard: the Lord stays as a silent body, or the knower becomes a silent body in which the Lord stays. Either way knowing ends in silence, not in recitation.

983.reading: Because the two conches and the one stream are finely entangled, how many humans in the world dim and die? If you can set aside the two conches and blow the stream, you may live united with the one who shares his body with the breasted woman.
983.nuance: A cipher verse. Tradition reads சங்கு இரண்டு (two conches) as the two nostrils or the two side channels, ida and pingala, and தாரை ஒன்று (one stream) as the central channel; ஊதல் (blowing) is then driving the breath up the middle. On a plain reading the words are conches and a pipe, and the verse is unreadable, so the coded reading carries it.

984.reading: Born in the five letters, grown in the five letters, you recite the five letters, sinners made of the five elements; if you can know and say the one letter among the five, the Lord dances in the hall saying 'fear not, fear not'.
984.nuance: The five letters and the five elements are set side by side, so the reciters are made of what they recite. ஓர் எழுத்து, the one letter, is not named; tradition takes it as சி, or as the five held as one, as in Tirumanthiram 2720.

985.reading: Five and five and five; the beginningless too is five; is it not unripe, madmen, what you babble? If you can hold the five in your heart and stand joined, there is no five and no six; it appears as the beginningless.
985.nuance: The fives are not named: tradition supplies the five letters, the five elements and the five senses, or the fives of the tattva lists. பிஞ்சு (unripe) is the poet's word for the others' understanding. The last line empties the numbers once the five are held.

986.reading: You build long houses and shut tall doors; is it because you want to live, rejoicing people? When the sound of Death comes, all stand with hands wrung; the feet of the one who ate the poison and the feet of the Mother are the truth.
986.nuance: கைகலந்து நின்றிடும் can be hands joined in helpless appeal or kin standing mingled in grief. The oath line closes as at 968.

987.reading: While the boat lasts you can run about on the water; while the boat lasts you can make yourself firm; when the boat has broken, in the matchless open there is no play, no pole and no one at all.
987.nuance: The boat is the body and உறுதி பண்ணுதல் the securing of release while it lasts. ஆடும் இல்லை கோலும் இல்லை is read as no dance or play and no pole or oar; ஒப்பிலாத வெளி (the matchless open) is the void after the body goes, with no one left in it. The verse does not say whether that void is release or mere nothing.

988.reading: People who build houses, perform sacrifices, mix truth with falsehood and think 'cattle, children, wife, kin': when the summons comes in the hand of the Arbiter who holds the land, this body will not fetch the price of a potsherd.
988.nuance: ஓலை is the palm-leaf summons, and நடுவர் Yama as at 969. Sacrifice is listed with house-building and family as one more possession.

links.note: Both make the five letters the container of the world: Tirumular says by them the Lord made the elements, the wombs of birth and the wide world; Sivavakkiyar says the cosmos and beyond, the three gods and the letters of Om are all held within them.

The same siddhi with the same proof: Tirumular sets the two breaths in the upper palate so that grey hair and wrinkles change and one becomes a child; Sivavakkiyar raises the breath from the channel to the skull so that the old become children and the body reddens. Both seal it with Nandi's or the Mother's authority.

Both follow the body to the cremation ground and no further: Tirumular's town wails, burns the corpse, bathes and stops thinking of him; Sivavakkiyar's fine body stinks and is handed to the cremation keeper. Sivavakkiyar adds the jealous man ready to kill for a body that ends this way.

Tirumular says that even having recited, people are mutes who know nothing unless they join the beginning and the end; Sivavakkiyar asks the sastra-reciter whether the Veda will help when the death-sweat comes, and sets a moment's inner knowing against the whole scripture-bag.

Ghee within milk is in both the figure for the Lord present but unseen: Tirumular says the Stainless one is there as ghee in milk yet they do not desire that light; Sivavakkiyar says the Veda-reciters do not know the Lord within them as ghee hidden in milk.

Both say recitation of the Lord's letters removes what binds: Tirumular's SIVAYANAMA makes the three impurities cry out and leave; Sivavakkiyar's five-and-three mantra makes a hundred crore of the five great sins fly like cotton. Tirumular speaks of mala, Sivavakkiyar of sins, so the thing removed differs.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge; Sivavakkiyar says the Sama and four Vedas and all the sastras, recited in safety, leave one not knowing Siva. Both deny learning any worth apart from the Lord, though Sivavakkiyar's route is inward perception, not bowing.

Read as cipher, both describe one practice: Arunagirinathar asks that the breath be run from the root through ida, pingala and the middle way up the pillar; Sivavakkiyar says set aside the two conches and blow the one stream, and union follows. The Thiruppugazh names the channels; Sivavakkiyar codes them.

Both set one letter above the recited Vedas: Tirumular says what is ours lies in one letter of our Lord, and mastering it brings one to the far shore; Sivavakkiyar says that knowing the one letter among the five brings the Dancer's 'fear not'. Neither names the letter.

Tirumular says those who recite the first of the Dancer's letters stand as one in creed with him, and that is the sign for seeing the Dancer; Sivavakkiyar says the one who knows the one letter sees the Lord dance in the hall. Both make a single letter the condition of seeing the dance.

The Naladiyar says no one has leapt clear of Death and tomorrow the funeral drum may sound; Sivavakkiyar asks the builders of long houses with shut doors whether they mean to live, and shows them standing helpless when Death's sound comes. The Naladiyar draws the lesson of giving, Sivavakkiyar of holding to the feet.

Both say use the body while it lasts: the Naladiyar tells those with a sturdy body to take the fruit it can yield before it departs like mist; Sivavakkiyar says make yourself firm while the boat lasts, for when it breaks there is no one left in the open.

Both price the body at death at nothing: Arunagirinathar's body, after the whole life from womb to pyre, is not worth a handful of ash; Sivavakkiyar's, when Yama's summons comes, will not fetch the price of a potsherd. Sivavakkiyar adds that sacrifice and household are counted among the same possessions.

source_issues: The section labels printed beside the ids (அக்ஷர நிலை, சரியை விலக்கல், யோக நிலை and the rest) are a modern editor's headings, not the poet's; they do not group the verses in the text and 970 to 976 under ஞான நிலை include the ராம verses that tradition disputes.
983 line 2 is spaced மங்கிமாளு தேஉலகில் for மங்கிமாளுதே உலகில்.
